title: Piku Learns to Share

scenes.summary: Piku the panda loves food but does not like sharing.
scenes.text:
Piku the Panda Who Didn’t Like Sharing

In a peaceful bamboo forest, lived a cuddly little panda named Piku.

Piku loved to eat.

Crunchy bamboo, juicy apples, sweet berries—he loved them all!

But there was one thing Piku did not like…

Sharing his food.
scenes.image_prompt: cute panda holding food in bamboo forest, bright cheerful cartoon style

scenes.summary: Piku refuses to share his apple with Momo, making his friend sad.
scenes.text:
Whenever Piku found something tasty, he kept it all to himself.

One day, he found a big, shiny red apple.

“Wow! This is mine!” he said happily.

Just then, his friend Momo the Monkey came by.

“Can I have a small piece?” Momo asked.

Piku hugged the apple tightly.

“No! It’s all mine!”

Momo looked sad and walked away.
scenes.image_prompt: panda hugging red apple while monkey looks sad, forest setting, cartoon style

scenes.summary: Piku feels lonely and faces trouble during a sudden rain.
scenes.text:
Later, Piku sat under a tree and ate his apple.

Crunch! Crunch!

But something felt strange.

It didn’t taste as good as he expected.

He looked around.

No one was there.

“I wish someone was here,” Piku said softly.

Suddenly, dark clouds filled the sky.

Rain began to pour.

Drip! Drop! Splash!

Piku ran to find shelter.

But all the good spots were already taken.
scenes.image_prompt: panda sitting alone eating apple then running in rain looking worried, colorful cartoon

scenes.summary: Momo kindly offers shelter, and Piku realizes his mistake.
scenes.text:
Just then, Piku saw Momo sitting under a big tree.

There was space beside him.

Piku hesitated.

“Can I sit here?” he asked quietly.

Momo smiled.

“Of course, Piku!”

Piku sat down, feeling a little shy.

Piku remembered the apple.

“I didn’t share with Momo,” he thought.

He felt sorry.

“I’m sorry,” Piku said. “Next time, I will share.”

Momo smiled.

“That’s okay,” he said kindly.

“We can share the shelter now.”
scenes.image_prompt: monkey sharing shelter with panda under tree in rain, warm friendly cartoon scene

scenes.summary: Piku learns to share and enjoys food more with his friend.
scenes.text:
The next day, Piku found some berries.

This time, he called out,

“Momo! Come share with me!”

They sat together and ate happily.

The berries tasted sweeter than ever.

Sharing makes things more joyful.

It’s always better to enjoy things together.

The End
scenes.image_prompt: panda and monkey happily sharing berries together in forest, bright joyful cartoon style

story:
Piku the Panda Who Didn’t Like Sharing

In a peaceful bamboo forest, lived a cuddly little panda named Piku.

Piku loved to eat.

Crunchy bamboo, juicy apples, sweet berries—he loved them all!

But there was one thing Piku did not like…

Sharing his food.

Whenever Piku found something tasty, he kept it all to himself.

One day, he found a big, shiny red apple.

“Wow! This is mine!” he said happily.

Just then, his friend Momo the Monkey came by.

“Can I have a small piece?” Momo asked.

Piku hugged the apple tightly.

“No! It’s all mine!”

Momo looked sad and walked away.

Later, Piku sat under a tree and ate his apple.

Crunch! Crunch!

But something felt strange.

It didn’t taste as good as he expected.

He looked around.

No one was there.

“I wish someone was here,” Piku said softly.

Suddenly, dark clouds filled the sky.

Rain began to pour.

Drip! Drop! Splash!

Piku ran to find shelter.

But all the good spots were already taken.

Just then, Piku saw Momo sitting under a big tree.

There was space beside him.

Piku hesitated.

“Can I sit here?” he asked quietly.

Momo smiled.

“Of course, Piku!”

Piku sat down, feeling a little shy.

Piku remembered the apple.

“I didn’t share with Momo,” he thought.

He felt sorry.

“I’m sorry,” Piku said. “Next time, I will share.”

Momo smiled.

“That’s okay,” he said kindly.

“We can share the shelter now.”

The next day, Piku found some berries.

This time, he called out,

“Momo! Come share with me!”

They sat together and ate happily.

The berries tasted sweeter than ever.

Sharing makes things more joyful.

It’s always better to enjoy things together.

The End
